To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have investigated parametric generation of light pulses of high quality (τΔν≤1) in the range of 0.672 to 2.56 μ m, by pumping an optical resonator by the harmonic radiation from an actively mode-locked Q-switched laser.
we have developed a new technique of synchronously pumped parametric generation with picosecond light pulse of high spectral quality.
we have developed an optical parametric amplifier that can generate high quality, picosecond pulses in the 1.2 to 3.5 micrometer wavelength range.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new method of generating tunable picosecond radiation of high spectral quality and with the investigation of the properties of an optical parametric generator with a dispersive cavity.
the investigation of the properties of an optical parametric amplifier with a dispersive cavity pumped with radiation from a synchronously pumped optical parametric oscillator.
a study of a novel class of optical parametric oscillators, which can be used as sources of picosecond radiation of high spectral quality in the range of wavelengths from 0.67 μm to 2.5 μm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results obtained are of great interest in terms of both the fundamental and applied aspects of physics and technology.
the results of the present investigation are of fundamental importance for the study of nonlinear optical phenomena and for the development of new types of picosecond lasers and optical systems.
the authors have succeeded in demonstrating a new and interesting approach to the development of high quality, high efficiency, tunable picosecond light sources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an optical parametric generator of high-quality picosecond light with a wide range of wavelengths and with an efficiency of 8.1%.
the optical parametric oscillator described above is the most efficient and the most compact device for generation of high-quality picosecond pulses in the spectral region from 0.672 to 2.56 μM.

we have demonstrated a new type of picosecond optical parametric oscillator which is based on the synchronously pumped dispersive resonator and is capable to generate high-quality picosecond pulses of high energy in a broad spectral range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optical parametric oscillator can be used as a picosecond source of high-quality radiation with a wide tunability range and high efficiency.

the use of a dispersive resonant cavity in the optical parametric oscillator allows one to obtain picosecond light radiation of high spectral purity and to reduce the threshold for parametric oscillation by a factor of 10.
the use of a dispersive resonant scheme for the parametric oscillator makes it possible to obtain high-quality picosecond radiation with a wide tuning range of wavelengths.  (1)
